chunks: 4 - He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi reported to me, he said: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Umar ibn Isa ibn Uthman narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, he said: Khalid ibn Amir ibn Abbas narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Swaid al-Ash'ari who said:

Fatr ibn Khalifa and I visited Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He brought us some dates which we ate, and he kept giving some to Fatr. Then he said to him: "What about the tradition which you narrated to me from Abu al-Tufail, may Allah have mercy on him, regarding the Abdal?" Fatr said: I heard Abu al-Tufail say: I heard Ali, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) say: "The Abdal are from the people of Sham and the noble ones are from the people of Kufa. Allah will gather them on a day that will be the worst for our enemies."

Then Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: "May Allah have mercy on you. With us begins the trial, then with you; and with us begins the relief, then with you. May Allah have mercy on whoever endears us to the people and does not cause them to detest us."

key_terms.الأبدال: Abdal (the Substitutes/Saints) - a spiritual rank of righteous people who uphold the world
key_terms.البلاء: Trial/severe test - refers to the afflictions that befall the Ahlul Bayt and their followers
key_terms.الرخاء: Relief/ease - the eventual divine relief that also begins with the Ahlul Bayt
key_terms.النجباء: Nujaba (the Noble Ones) - a rank of spiritual elites, closely associated with the Shia heartland of Kufa

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali and Imam Sadiq say about the Abdal saints and the people of Sham and Kufa?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Amali of al-Mufid, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) comments on a tradition from Imam Ali (AS) about the Abdal (spiritual saints) of Sham and the Nujaba (noble ones) of Kufa, whom Allah will rally against the enemies. The Imam affirms that trials and relief both begin with the Ahlul Bayt before reaching their followers, and prays for those who make people love them rather than causing resentment. This narration was shared in an intimate gathering where the Imam served dates to his guests, reflecting the personal and spiritual bond between the Imam and his companions.
